concepts.title: Measures of Central Tendency: Mean
concepts.definition: The mean is the plain average of a numeric column: pool every observation, add them, and share the total equally among the count of values. One unusually large or small reading (an outlier) drags the mean toward itself, so such readings are often dropped first.
concepts.key_idea: Add all the readings once, divide once by how many there are; beware outliers before trusting the result.
question_patterns: find the mean height of the class with readings 90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110, 110 cm
calculate the average temperature of the week from 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34 degrees
why is the mean a poor choice when outliers are present in the data
the total of 9 heights is 912 cm; what is the average height
define mean and state one situation where it misleads
a class of 40 students has a total weight of 2200 kg; find the mean weight

solution_steps.action: pool the readings into one total
solution_steps.explain: sum() adds every observation of the attribute in one sweep
solution_steps.compute: data_total = sum((reading_one, reading_two, reading_three, reading_four, reading_five, reading_six, reading_seven, reading_eight, reading_nine))

solution_steps.explain: dividing by the number of observations gives the average

worked_examples.q: Four readings are 10, 20, 30 and 60. What is their mean?

concepts.title: Median of Sorted Data
concepts.definition: The median is the midpoint of the data once the values are arranged in order: with an odd count it is simply the value at the central position, and with an even count it is the average of the two values straddling the middle. Unlike the mean, it ignores how extreme the end values are.
concepts.key_idea: Sort first; for n values the middle seat is (n + 1) // 2 when n is odd, and the pair around it is averaged when n is even.
question_patterns: find the median height of the sorted data 85, 90, 90, 100, 102, 110, 110, 110, 115
which position holds the median when the data has 9 values
how is the median obtained when the number of values is even
why is the median less affected by outliers than the mean
find the median temperature of the week 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34
state the first step required before the median can be computed

solution_steps.explain: for an even count n, integer division by 2 gives the lower of the two central positions
the second central value sits immediately after the first
the median of an even-sized batch is the mean of the pair straddling the middle

worked_examples.q: Sorted values 12, 15, 40: what is the median?

concepts.title: Mode and Frequency Share
concepts.definition: The mode is the value that shows up most often in the data, judged purely by how frequently each distinct value occurs. A set where every value appears once has no mode, and several values tying at the top give multiple modes; the mode works for non-numeric labels too.
concepts.key_idea: Count how often each value appears; the winner is the mode, and its count over the total tells how dominant it is.
question_patterns: which value is the mode of the heights 90, 102, 110, 115, 85, 90, 100, 110, 110 and how often does it occur
what percentage of the 9 height observations does the mode 110 represent
when does a data set have no mode
can there be more than one mode in a data set
find the mode of the weekly temperatures 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34

solution_steps.explain: max() over the occurrence counts of the candidate values finds the mode's frequency

solution_steps.action: express it as a share of all observations
solution_steps.explain: dividing by the total number of observations and scaling by 100 gives the mode's dominance in percent

worked_examples.q: In the column 5, 7, 7, 9, which value is the mode?

concepts.title: Range as Maximum minus Minimum
concepts.definition: The range is the simplest spread measure for numeric data: subtract the smallest reading from the largest. It depends only on the two extremes, so a single outlier inflates it dramatically.
concepts.key_idea: Largest value minus smallest value; cheap to compute but hostage to the extremes.
question_patterns: find the range of the heights when the minimum is 85 cm and the maximum is 115 cm
calculate the temperature range of the week from 34, 34, 27, 28, 27, 34, 34
why does an outlier badly influence the range
for which kind of data can the range be calculated
the salaries in an office run from 15000 to 90000; state the range
which two values of the data does the range use

solution_steps.explain: max() returns the biggest value among the observations
solution_steps.compute: tallest_value = max((reading_one, reading_two, reading_three, reading_four, reading_five))

solution_steps.explain: min() returns the smallest value among the observations
solution_steps.compute: shortest_value = min((reading_one, reading_two, reading_three, reading_four, reading_five))

solution_steps.explain: the spread between the two ends is the range

worked_examples.q: Readings span 15 cm to 45 cm. What is the range in cm?

concepts.title: Standard Deviation of a Data Set
concepts.definition: Standard deviation measures how far the readings stray from their mean on average: take each value's gap from the mean, square the gaps, average them, and take the positive square root. A small result means tightly packed data, a large one means wide scatter, and unlike the range it uses every reading.
concepts.key_idea: Square the gaps from the mean, average them, then root the average; every value contributes, not just the extremes.
concepts.textbook_ref: keip105.txt section 5.5.2 B, Example 5.5 and Table 5.3 (lines 595-710)
question_patterns: compute the standard deviation when the sum of squared deviations is 938 for 9 height readings

which greek letter represents standard deviation in the chapter

solution_steps.explain: dividing the sum of squared deviations by the number of observations gives the variance
sqrt of the variance brings the spread back to the data's own units

worked_examples.q: Which spread measure uses every reading rather than only the extremes?

concepts.title: Structured, Unstructured Data and Metadata
concepts.definition: Data that fits a fixed row-and-column arrangement, with each column an attribute and each row one observation, is structured. Newspaper pages, emails and multimedia files have no such fixed shape and are unstructured; they are described indirectly through metadata, which is descriptive data about data such as an image's size, type and resolution.
concepts.key_idea: Tables hold structured data with named attributes; everything shapeless needs metadata to describe it.
question_patterns: differentiate between structured and unstructured data with one example of each
is the content of an email structured or unstructured data
what is metadata? give the metadata of an image file
in a table of kitchen items, what does one column and one row represent
which attributes describe an email as metadata

solution_steps.action: test for a fixed row-column shape
solution_steps.explain: data arranging neatly into named columns and observation rows is structured
free text, images, audio and video without a fixed layout are unstructured
metadata such as file size, format and resolution summarises unstructured content

worked_examples.q: An image's size, type and resolution describe it indirectly. What is such descriptive data called?

concepts.title: Data Processing Cycle: Input to Output
concepts.definition: Raw facts become usable conclusions only through the data processing cycle: collect and enter the raw data, store it, classify and update it, process it, and finally present reports or results as output. An ATM withdrawal, an online admit card or a train ticket all follow this input-process-output path.
concepts.key_idea: Data in, operations applied, information out; storage and retrieval support every stage.
question_patterns: draw the steps of the data processing cycle for an ATM cash withdrawal
what inputs, processing and outputs are involved in issuing a train ticket
why can decisions not be taken by merely looking at raw data
name the three broad stages shown in the data process cycle figure
list the data required to generate an examination admit card online
how does a database management system overcome the limits of file processing

solution_steps.explain: inputs are the collected raw data, like card number and amount for a withdrawal
processing validates the input, updates balances or allots seats, and prepares results
outputs are the currency with a slip, the admit card, or the printed ticket

worked_examples.q: In the data processing cycle, what stage follows processing: input or output?
